newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares static in dead market, outlook same.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares static in dead market, outlook same.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly down but virtually unchanged on Friday in a moribund market suffering from a dearth of players, with dealers painting much the same picture for Monday.
"It was a very dull day without any activity of note. It was impossible to find a seller on the market and the outlook for the start of next week looks just as dismal," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed a marginal 0.07 point down at 122.73. The KFX December future remained untraded throughout the day at 123.65.
Dealers also said foreign investors indulged in a certain amount of profit-taking at the end of the day when the market began to show signs of reviving a little.

Banks were mixed despite the generally solid bond market with Den Danske Bank shedding one crown to finish at 430, rival Unibank closing unchanged and third biggest BG Bank putting on two crowns to end up at 225.
Tele Danmark was again much in focus with 227,000 shares changing hands to close one crown up at 279.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.008 billion crowns.
